FROM "lines" AS t0
  JOIN "orders" AS j1 ON t0."order_id" = j1."order_id"
  JOIN "customers" AS j2 ON j1."customer_id" = j2."customer_id"
  JOIN "products" AS j3 ON t0."product_id" = j3."product_id"
WHERE j3."category" IN ('A')
  AND t0."order_id" IN (
SELECT DISTINCT s0."order_id" FROM "payments" AS s0
  
WHERE s0."method" IN ('card', 'bank')
)
GROUP BY j2."region"

combination.merge: per-fact results are merged on the group key; each fact is aggregated in its own SQL statement, so no fact row is ever counted through another fact

ratios.rule: recomputed per output group: numerator/denominator; denominator == 0 yields the model's zero_denominator
recomputed per output group: numerator/denominator; denominator == 0 yields the model's zero_denominator

why_no_double_count: Each fact is read by its own single-fact aggregation statement; orders/lines/payments are never in the same FROM clause.
Every dimension join follows only declared many_to_one edges, so joining a dimension cannot multiply fact rows.
entity_exists is computed once as an order-id set (intersected across entity filters) and applied as a key restriction; it does not copy filter predicates onto unrelated facts.
local filters appear only in the WHERE clause of their own fact's aggregation.
The final combination is a keyed union: a group missing from a fact receives the model's empty_measure (0), never a duplicate row.
